summary: Streaming disconnect spikes in us-east not reflected on public status page (status remained green)
description:
Customer report (Northbridge AI Platform, enterprise):

Issue summary:
- Beginning ~2025-11-21 09:05 PT, customer observed elevated streaming disconnects for chat completions in us-east.
- Impacted traffic was primarily streaming (SSE). Non-streaming responses were reported as “mostly OK” with intermittent latency.
- Public status page showed all components operational during the impact window; customer is asking why the incident was not communicated and requesting per-capability visibility (Streaming vs non-streaming).

Customer impact:
- Customer’s end users experienced partial responses / dropped connections while waiting for streamed tokens.
- Customer’s app retries increased significantly; they estimate ~6–10% of sessions required a user refresh.

Environment:
- Prod
- Region: us-east

Customer notes / evidence:
- “We see spike in `ERR_STREAM_CLOSED` / client disconnects between 09:05–09:40 PT. Status page stayed green; support macros told us to check status page first and it wasn’t helpful.”
- Example request details provided by customer (redacted): request_id prefixes `nb-9f2*`, `nb-a31*`.

Requested outcome:
1) Confirm whether Redwood had a known incident in us-east affecting streaming.
2) Clarify whether this should have been on the status page.
3) Provide guidance/workaround and expected prevention.
4) Improve status page granularity so streaming-only failures are communicated clearly.

Internal notes (initial triage):
- Likely a streaming-specific failure mode (disconnects at gateway or websocket/SSE path) that doesn’t manifest as elevated 5xx for non-streaming requests.
- Current public component grouping is too coarse (Hosted API rolled up), and current status signal is primarily error-rate based; streaming disconnect counters are not part of the status signal source-of-truth today.
comments:
[2025-11-21 09:28 PT] Rachel Kim (Reporter, Enterprise CS)
Customer pinged QBR follow-up thread; escalating as status-page accuracy issue. They are blocked on explaining internally why status page was green.

[2025-11-21 09:41 PT] Dev Patel (Assignee, Support)
Acknowledged. Pulling logs/metrics for us-east streaming path. Looping in #incidents and SRE on-call for verification. Asking customer for 2–3 request_ids and timestamps (PT + UTC).

[2025-11-21 10:03 PT] Rachel Kim (Enterprise CS)
Customer provided timestamps (PT) and 3 request IDs (sent via secure channel). They confirmed SDK: JS v2.8.1, streaming enabled, max_tokens 800, average prompt ~1.2k tokens. Retries: 2 with jitter.

[2025-11-21 10:20 PT] Dev Patel (Support)
Internal checks:
- Gateway 5xx and overall request success rate looks within baseline for Hosted API in us-east.
- However, streaming disconnect counter is elevated (suspected) but current dashboard does not break out by region + capability. Looping Observability.

[2025-11-21 10:27 PT] Allison Grant (Observability)
Confirmed: we have some streaming disconnect telemetry but it’s not consistently tagged by region/capability in the default dashboards. This matches a known gap. We can validate via raw metric queries, but status automation won’t trigger because it’s not in the public-signal mapping.

[2025-11-21 10:34 PT] Rafael Mendes (SRE)
On-call context: We saw a transient increase in streaming disconnects in us-east around 16:05–16:40 UTC consistent with a backend connection churn event. Because error-rate SLOs didn’t burn and overall API success remained high, we did not declare a public incident.
This is exactly the class of “streaming-only degradation” we want the new component taxonomy to cover.

[2025-11-21 10:48 PT] Dev Patel (Support) — Customer response drafted
Thanks for the detailed timestamps. We’re investigating a us-east issue that can affect streaming connections (SSE) without materially changing non-streaming success rates. We’ll follow up with findings and a short summary suitable for internal reporting. In the meantime, recommended mitigations:
- Ensure client uses keep-alive and supports reconnect/resume behavior.
- Add retry with exponential backoff for stream initiation failures.
- Consider temporarily falling back to non-streaming for the most latency-tolerant paths.

[2025-11-21 11:12 PT] Christine Wong (Status transparency implementer)
Noted for transparency upgrades: current status page doesn’t have a streaming capability component per region, so we have no place to mark “Hosted API – Streaming – us-east” as degraded. This ticket is a good customer example for the rollout/training deck.

[2025-11-21 11:35 PT] Dev Patel (Support)
Action items proposed:
1) Confirm exact impact window with SRE and provide customer-facing post-incident summary (publishable, not overly detailed).
2) Add streaming disconnect signal into the component-level health dashboards for us-east.
3) Update status-page component taxonomy to include Streaming (by region) and map signals accordingly.

[2025-11-22 08:10 PT] Irene Choi (Infra)
We can reproduce similar behavior in a load test when upstream connection pools churn; it manifests as client disconnects, not necessarily 5xx. Fix likely belongs to streaming edge handling (graceful reconnect + timeout tuning) and better detection.

[2025-11-22 09:02 PT] Dev Patel (Support) — Customer update
We confirmed an internal event in us-east that increased streaming disconnects for a subset of requests during the reported window. Overall API success metrics did not exceed incident thresholds, which is why the public status page remained green.
We agree that this is not ideal for customers who rely on streaming; we are implementing streaming-specific status components and signals so future streaming-only degradations are reflected more accurately.

[2025-11-25 14:20 PT] Aisha Bello (SLO dashboards)
FYI: we’re adding region-aware streaming health panels and aligning naming to status components. Once deployed, Support can reference a stable dashboard link for disputes.

[2025-11-28 09:18 PT] Dev Patel (Support)
Customer accepted summary + mitigation guidance. They asked for confirmation that we will publish post-incident summaries going forward; pointed them to upcoming policy and that we’ll share a link once the format is live.
resolution:
Resolved as “status reporting gap + streaming-specific signal gap” (not a single-customer issue).

What happened:
- Short-lived us-east event caused elevated streaming disconnects (SSE) without significant changes in overall Hosted API 5xx/error-rate signals.
- Public status page stayed green because current components/signals are too coarse and are primarily error-rate based.

Customer-facing outcome:
- Provided customer a concise, publishable summary of the window and recommended mitigations (retry/backoff, fallback to non-streaming where acceptable).

Follow-ups (tracked outside this ticket):
- Add region-aware streaming error/disconnect telemetry and dashboards.
- Introduce streaming-specific public status components and map internal signals to them as part of Status Page Transparency Upgrades.

Close criteria:
- Customer acknowledged receipt and confirmed mitigations; internal owners captured as inputs to the ongoing transparency upgrades workstream.
